newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end down 1/2 to 3/4.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end down 1/2 to 3/4.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices ended down 1/2 to 3/4 of a point Friday as the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond managed to mend some of the deep price cuts inflicted by the morning's strong jobs report.

"I'd say we are down 1/2 because there has been some business going on," a municipal trader said. "I don't think people are whacking cash as much as they are futures...I think there were probably more bottom fishers and less sellers, therefore I don't think the cash market was down as much as the futures market was."
The March municipal futures contract closed down 25/32 at 114-10/32. The March T-bond contract closed down 1-2/32 at 110-11/32. The MOB spread was 127 ticks.
A municipal analyst, however, said muni cash ended down 3/4 of a point overall. Dollar bond losses mirrored the broader market, while high-grade issues worsened by about seven basis points, he said.
Dollar bonds had been down about 7/8 of a point until roughtly 1515 EST, the analyst said. At its lowest point point, the overall muni cash market was cuffed down about a point, he said.

In the government cash market, the benchmark 30-year bond closed down 1-6/32 at 95-19/32 to yield 6.85 percent. Bonds were hit hard after the Labor Department said the U.S. economy created 262,000 jobs in December, versus economists' predictions of a 192,000 gain.

Turning to new issues, scheduled competitive and negotiated municipal bond sales for the week of Jan 13 are expected to total $3.2 billion in 105 offerings, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Competitive sales are expected to total $987 million million in 64 sales. The largest is a $195 million North Carolina revenue bond deal on Wednesday.
Negotiated sales are expected to total $2.2 billion in 41 offerings. The largest is a $550 million New York City general obligation deal through Goldman Sachs & Co.
An additional $538 million of deals are on the possible list, meaning underwriters have said they may price the deal sometime next week depending on market conditions.
